rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heavy fan-out prompts get body recovery callout
rules_evaluated.evidence: P4's walk-down prompt says 'walk down EVERY unresolved branch' and reads the codebase per-question - documented in the maintainer block as a real overrun risk (2026-05-15 dry-run: 13m15s/37.7K tokens on one turn). Harm the rule guards against: a shallow pass gets accepted as 'done' because fluent output masks a premature stop. The over-reading direction IS covered ('If it feels sluggish, ask why... relax the requirement'), but no body language nudges the student to push Claude to keep going if the walk-down stops short of 'every' branch - only when-to-stop guidance exists, not when-to-push-further guidance. Harm is real but attenuated: the mechanic is turn-by-turn and human-in-the-loop (student sees each batch of 3, unlike a silent autonomous audit), which is the file's own structural mitigation rule 48 doesn't anticipate for interactive rather than single-shot fan-out.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: One sentence near 'Answer the branches...' or the Stop-when-reaching callout: if the walk-down seems to wrap up early on a plan that clearly has more surface, ask 'what else is unresolved here?' before moving on.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Pre-action framing doesn't preview prompt's payoff
rules_evaluated.evidence: Current L7 ('What you build') reads 'A second-pass walk-down, three questions at a time' - names ACTIVITY only (axis b, KEEP), no REVEAL/SHOW/SURFACE/PRODUCE language. The value-claim clause ('catches the branches you can't see') is no longer in the pre-action opener at all; it now lives post-action in the P5 'Compare what each read caught' section ('The second read catches what an agent walking a decision tree catches: branches you didn't notice...'), which is exactly where §53 wants it. Phase 5's own opener (before {{prompt:push-back-on-the-plan-3}}) asks Claude to 'compare what the second-pass read surfaced against what your two push-backs caught' without naming what specifically will be found - no pre-announcement. Note: the maintainer accept-note at L124 ('What-you-build keeps catches the branches you can't see') is now itself stale as a literal description - the quoted clause isn't in the What-you-build line anymore, though the underlying design goal it defended has been met via relocation, not violated. Flagging for the maintainer to refresh the note's wording, not as a body-content REVISE.
